source_statement: THIS CONTRACT IS DERIVED FROM REFERENCE DOCUMENTATION, NOT FROM A PUBLISHED SPECIFICATION. VCF Automation (the VCF 9.1 successor to vRealize Automation and Aria Automation) has no specification in the vmware/vcf-api-specs repository and ships no machine-readable OpenAPI document on the Broadcom Developer Portal. Every path, method, header, field, type, requirement flag and status code below was transcribed by hand on 2026-08-11 from the human-readable xAPIs reference pages recorded in docs/official_sources.json. Where this file states something the reference pages do not literally say, the entry carries "derivation": "inferred" and explains the reasoning. Do not treat this file as vendor-published truth; treat it as a reviewed transcription that may drift from the appliance.

server.description: VCF Automation appliance FQDN. The loopback mock in tests/vcfa_mock.py substitutes a 127.0.0.1 origin; no live VMware endpoint is contacted by this repository.

wire_rules.derivation_note: The reference pages literally identify bearer authentication and application/json request bodies, but do not define charset, Accept-header, absent-value, unknown-field or unset-query behavior. Those rules are local contract commitments for this client and are not represented as vendor-published requirements.
wire_rules.optional_field_handling: An optional field that the caller did not set MUST be omitted from the request body entirely. It MUST NOT be serialised as null, as an empty string, or as an empty object. The appliance distinguishes 'absent' from 'explicitly cleared', so sending an empty value is a different request than sending none.
wire_rules.unknown_fields: Only the fields marked writable in the schemas below may appear in a request body. Server-managed read-only fields must never be sent back.
wire_rules.query_string: Query parameters that the caller did not set MUST be omitted; requests must not carry an empty query string or parameters with empty values.

operations.name: Create Policy
operations.summary: Creates a new policy, updates an existing policy, or trigger a policy dry-run.

idempotency.rule: Send the caller's stable policy id in the request body's `id` field on every attempt, including retries. Because the operation is documented as create-or-update, a retry that carries the same `id` overwrites the same policy instead of creating a second one. A request that omits `id` is NOT retry-safe: the appliance mints a fresh policy id per accepted request, so a retry after a lost response leaves two policies behind.
idempotency.derivation_note: The reference page does not use the words 'idempotent' or 'retry'. This rule is inferred from two documented facts on that page: the operation summary is 'Creates a new policy, updates an existing policy, ...', and `id` (string, uuid) is listed as an accepted, optional field of the request body schema rather than as a read-only response field.
idempotency.retry_note: The documented success responses carry no body, so a client cannot tell an applied-but-lost 5xx from a rejected one. It must retry and rely on the `id` for convergence.

query_parameters.name: validationOnly
query_parameters.description: For a dry run that will do policy validation only.

responses.body_note: The reference page states the operation does not return a data structure for 200, 201 or 202. Read the policy back with getPolicy to observe the stored state.

responses.description: Bad Request - request body failed business-rule validation.

Policy.description: Policy object. Used both as the createOrUpdatePolicy request body and as the getPolicy response body.
Policy.derivation_note: Field names, types and required flags are transcribed from the reference page. Writable flags are local inferences: the page presents one Policy shape for both mutation and read responses even though timestamps, author/editor expansions, legends and statistics are server-managed.

fields.name: typeId
fields.description: The policy type id, for example com.vmware.policy.deployment.lease.

fields.name: id
fields.description: Policy id. Supplying it turns the create into an update of that policy; omitting it makes the appliance mint one.

fields.name: enforcementType
fields.description: Defines enforcement type for policy. Default enforcement type is HARD.

fields.name: definition
fields.description: Policy definition; its shape is dictated by the policy type's definitionSchema.

fields.name: criteria
fields.description: Policy-type-specific target object filter criteria applied during enforcement.

fields.name: opaRegoCriteria
fields.description: OPA Rego code applied during enforcement.

fields.name: projectId
fields.description: For project-scoped policies, the id of the project the policy belongs to.

fields.name: orgId
fields.description: Id of the organization the policy belongs to.

PolicyType.description: Policy type object returned by getPolicyType.

fields.name: definitionSchema
fields.description: Schema the policy definition must satisfy.

fields.name: config
fields.description: Policy type configuration: enableDryRun, enableEnforcementType, enableOpaRegoCriteria, enablePolicyValidation, enableReconciliation, enableSingleProjectScope, enableUpdateNotification, maxNumberOfPoliciesPerOrg, maxNumberOfPoliciesPerProject.

error.description: Error payload. The reference pages do not publish an error schema for these operations; the loopback mock emits {"message": string} and clients must not depend on the shape.
